query_text: Have any new literary genres emerged in this century?

action.query: 21st century new literary genres cli-fi litRPG solarpunk Twitterature
queries: 21st century new literary genres cli-fi litRPG solarpunk Twitterature

annotations.title: Climate Fiction, or ‘Cli-Fi,’ Is the Hottest New Literary Genre - GOOD
Twitterature: A New Digital Literary Genre | EVOLUTIONARY STUDIES IN IMAGINATIVE CULTURE

content.text:
Yes—but with a caveat: **literary genres rarely appear from nowhere**. Most “new” genres of the 21st century are better understood as **new labels, markets, and communities** crystallizing around older techniques or themes. That said, several recognizable genres/subgenres have emerged or become distinct this century.

### Examples

**1. Cli-fi / climate fiction**  
Fiction centered on climate change and ecological crisis. It has roots in earlier eco-fiction and science fiction, but the label and its broad literary identity gained traction in the 2000s–2010s. It now spans literary fiction, thrillers, dystopia, YA, and speculative fiction. ([good.is](https://www.good.is/articles/climate-fiction-cli-fi-genre?utm_source=openai))

**2. Solarpunk**  
A speculative genre/aesthetic imagining sustainable, socially just, often technologically inventive futures. It arose partly as a hopeful counterweight to cyberpunk, dystopia, and climate apocalypse narratives. It is still as much a movement and aesthetic as a book-market genre. ([solarpunkpress.net](https://solarpunkpress.net/about?utm_source=openai))

**3. LitRPG / progression fantasy**  
Fiction that incorporates role-playing-game mechanics—levels, stats, quests, skill trees—into the narrative. Its precursors are older, but LitRPG as a named genre and publishing category became especially visible in the 2010s, helped by online publishing, ebooks, audiobooks, and gaming culture. ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LitRPG?utm_source=openai))

**4. Twitterature / social-media fiction / microfiction forms**  
Very short literary works written for or shaped by platforms such as Twitter/X, Instagram, texting, email, and other digital interfaces. The broader tradition of flash fiction is older, but platform-native constraints and formats have produced new literary forms. ([esiculture.com](https://esiculture.com/index.php/esiculture/article/view/371?utm_source=openai))

**5. Digi-fiction / app-based and multimedia fiction**  
Works that combine prose with images, sound, hyperlinks, interactivity, chat logs, or platform-specific design. Electronic literature existed before 2000, but smartphones, web platforms, fan communities, and interactive apps have made these forms more visible in the 21st century.

**6. Romantasy as a major market category**  
Romance-fantasy hybrids long predate this century, but “romantasy” has recently become a powerful publishing and bookselling label, especially through BookTok and online fandom. It is less a wholly new genre than a newly consolidated commercial category.

**7. Hopepunk**  
A speculative-fiction mode emphasizing resistance, kindness, solidarity, and moral courage in bleak worlds. Like solarpunk, it is partly a reaction against grimdark and dystopian fiction. It is more of an ethos or subgenre than a rigid genre.

### So, have truly “new” genres emerged?

**Yes, in the practical sense**: new names, communities, shelves, awards, hashtags, publishing niches, and reader expectations have formed around cli-fi, solarpunk, LitRPG, digital fiction, and related forms.

**But not entirely from scratch**: most descend from older genres—science fiction, fantasy, eco-fiction, epistolary fiction, experimental literature, romance, horror, and serial fiction. What is new is the combination of **21st-century anxieties**—climate change, digital life, gaming, platform culture—with new distribution systems such as ebooks, audiobooks, web serials, social media, and online fandom.
